## Purpose and Public Entry Points
`tiktoken` is a Python library for fast, reversible byte-pair encoding (BPE) tokenization used with OpenAI model encodings. Users import `tiktoken`, retrieve an encoding by name or model, then encode text to integer tokens and decode tokens back to text. Public package exports and lookup entry points originate in `tiktoken/__init__.py`, with the principal API in `tiktoken/core.py`.

## Python API and Encoding Boundary
`Encoding` in `tiktoken/core.py` owns an encoding definition: regex splitting pattern, mergeable byte-pair ranks, and special-token mappings. It exposes normal and special-token-aware encode/decode operations, batching, and offset-related behavior. This layer is the stable Python-facing contract and delegates performance-sensitive BPE work to the native extension.

Paths: `tiktoken/core.py`, `tiktoken/__init__.py`

## Native Rust Tokenization Engine
The package is a mixed Python/Rust distribution. Rust code implements the performance-critical encoding primitives and is exposed to Python through bindings. The Python wrapper passes encoding tables and text/token inputs across this FFI boundary; native results return to `Encoding` for API-level handling.

Paths: `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/py.rs`

## Encoding Discovery and Construction
The registry resolves a requested encoding name into a lazily constructed `Encoding`. It discovers built-in and installed namespace-plugin modules under `tiktoken_ext`, reads each module’s `ENCODING_CONSTRUCTORS`, detects collisions, and caches constructed encodings. This is the extension boundary for third parties: plugins provide constructor arguments rather than modifying core tokenization logic.

Paths: `tiktoken/registry.py`, `tiktoken_ext/openai_public.py`

## OpenAI Encoding Catalog and Model Mapping
Built-in OpenAI encoding constructors define regexes, token rank files, and special-token IDs. Model names are mapped to encoding names before dispatching through the registry. Thus `encoding_for_model()` follows: model lookup → encoding-name lookup → registry constructor → `Encoding` instance.

Paths: `tiktoken/model.py`, `tiktoken_ext/openai_public.py`, `tiktoken/registry.py`

## Vocabulary Asset Loading
Encoding constructors obtain mergeable-rank vocabularies through the loading subsystem. This separates remote/local asset retrieval, hashing/cache concerns, and vocabulary parsing from the core API and Rust engine. Constructed rank maps become immutable-ish input data for the encoder.

Paths: `tiktoken/load.py`, `tiktoken_ext/openai_public.py`

## Educational Implementation
A separate pure-Python educational module demonstrates BPE training and merge behavior. It supports learning and visualization but is not on the production fast path.

Paths: `tiktoken/_educational.py`

## Distribution and Runtime
Consumers run Python and install via PyPI; package build metadata combines Python packaging with Cargo/Rust compilation to produce platform wheels. Wheel CI is defined in `.github/workflows/build_wheels.yml`, making native-wheel production material to deployment.

Paths: `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `.github/workflows/build_wheels.yml`
